subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Find the amount of copper deposited at the electrode by passing 2 A of electricity for 10 minutes through a CuSO₄ solution.

verification.note: From the boxed 'PROBLEM' section of the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book p.72. A PROBLEM belongs to no printed paper section and the book prints no mark scheme for it, so both the Section-A placement and the 1+1 split are authored CLAIMS. Placed at 2 marks as a single-formula calculation; the same calculation at 1.5 A for 600 s is already authored at 4 marks as ts_ipe_c2_ec_cuso4_electrolysis_mass_of_copper, because the book asks it there as a Short Answer. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. THE BOOK IS WRONG HERE. It prints 'E(cu) = 63.5/2 = 31' and reaches 0.39 g. The equivalent mass of copper is 63.5/2 = 31.75, not 31, and with the correct value the answer is 31.75 × 2 × 600 / 96500 = 0.395 g. The card boxes 0.395 g and names the printed 31 and 0.39 g in the step's why so a student marked against the book is not stranded. The same error is recorded on ts_ipe_c2_ec_cuso4_electrolysis_mass_of_copper, whose insider note already tells the student not to copy the printed 31.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Equivalent mass and the relation
lines: Copper is deposited as Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu,
steps.why: Faraday's first law says the mass deposited is proportional to the quantity of electricity, and Q = i × t, which is why the current and the time appear as a product. The 96500 is the charge on one mole of electrons in coulombs, so dividing by it converts coulombs into equivalents. The valency is 2 because copper in copper sulphate is Cu²⁺ and needs two electrons per atom.
common_mistakes: Leaving the time in minutes. The 96500 is in coulombs, so the time must be in seconds.
Using 63.5 as the equivalent mass. That is the atomic mass; the equivalent mass divides it by the valency.
Taking the valency as 1. Copper is deposited from Cu²⁺, so two electrons are needed per atom.
steps.memory_tip: Equivalent mass is the atomic mass divided by the electrons needed: 63.5 over 2.
steps.margin_note: Convert the minutes to seconds and show the equivalent mass as a division. Both earn this mark.

steps.label: The mass deposited
steps.why: The three quantities on top multiply to 38100 coulomb-grams per equivalent, and dividing by the Faraday constant leaves a mass in grams. The book prints the equivalent mass as 31 rather than 31.75 and so reaches 0.39 g; the arithmetic here uses 31.75, which is what 63.5 divided by 2 actually is.
common_mistakes: Writing the equivalent mass as 31. 63.5 divided by 2 is 31.75, and the book's own printed 31 is an error.
Multiplying by 96500 instead of dividing. The Faraday constant is the denominator.
Leaving the answer without a unit. The mass is in grams.
steps.memory_tip: Top line is equivalent mass times current times seconds; the bottom line is always 96500.
steps.margin_note: Show 38100/96500 before the answer, and box the value in grams.

insider_note: Two marks, two traps: the time must be in seconds, and the equivalent mass is 63.5/2 = 31.75. This book prints 31 and gets 0.39 g — write 31.75 and 0.395 g, and show the division 63.5/2 so the examiner can see where the number came from.
